turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Sandip's arrogance is matched only by his ignorance, and it is high time he was made to understand that the zamindars of this region will not be intimidated by him.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala's gaze drifted between the two men, her expression a mask of calm interest.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip chuckled to himself, he said, Nikhil was so bent on being the great protector of the zamindars, but he had not protected his own tenants from Sandip's so-called oppression, had he?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Sandip's arrogance is but a thin veil for his own fear of being held accountable for his actions, and he would do well to remember that the zamindars of this region will not be cowed by his empty boasts.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip was wound up, he thought, as he gazed at Nikhil, and he wondered if Nikhil had ever stopped to think that maybe his own brand of zamindari was the real problem here, not some mythical threat from the Muslims.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Sandip's foolishness would be his own undoing, and it was a matter of time before the consequences of his actions came to light, and then he would see the true meaning of accountability.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Nikhil's warnings were as thick as the fog that clung to the riverbanks in winter, obscuring nothing, but merely adding to the mystique of his own self-importance.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Sandip's words were as empty as the promises of the monsoon rains, and it was a wonder he could speak with such conviction of his own invincibility.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Sandip's folly is not the only thing that will bring him down, for the zamindars of this region will not stand idly by while their lands are ravaged and their people suffer, and it is only a matter of time before the consequences of his actions come to light.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip's words dripped with sarcasm as he thought, Ha! Nikhil's threats were as potent as a snake's hiss in the dry autumn air, empty and harmless, and yet he persisted in trying to scare the wits out of him.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: The zamindars of this region have a long memory, and they will not forget the injustices inflicted upon them, nor will they stand idly by while their lands are ravaged.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: The words of Nikhil, though laced with foreboding, seemed to carry a hint of desperation, and she couldn't help but wonder what lay behind his urgency.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: The zamindars of this region will not be swayed by empty words and idle threats, and they will take decisive action to protect their lands and their people.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: It is intriguing, Nikhil, that the zamindars' collective memory is so long, yet their sense of justice seems fleeting.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: The zamindars of this region will not be intimidated by the rabble-rousing of a few Mussulman agitators, and they will stand firm in defense of their lands and their way of life.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip was exasperated, he thought, must Nikhil always be the harbinger of doom and gloom? Can't he see he was busy with his ghazals and hadn't a moment to spare for his dire prophecies?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: The zamindars have a sacred duty to protect their people and their lands, and they will not falter in this responsibility, no matter the threats or intimidation.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala's gaze drifted to Nikhil, her expression calm and inquiring, as she wondered if Sandip truly believed the zamindars could afford to be so dismissive of Nikhil's warnings.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip was dead tired, he told Nikhil, and he couldn't be bothered with some dusty old threat from the Mussulmans, not when he was busy with his poetry.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil was scathing in his assessment, his words dripping with disdain as he declared that the zamindars of this region had been plagued by the ravages of Mussulman depredations for far too long, precisely because of such foolishness.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Bimala where she would go, addressing her as the Queen.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he kept Browning among his books, reminding him of a contest they had over translating lines from Browning, and inquiring if Nikhil remembered it.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Nikhil and Bimala that he had managed to translate the lines into Bengali, but the result was unlikely to be well-received, and that he had once thought he was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence had intervened to prevent it, and he recalled old Dakshina's poetry.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Bimala that it was pointless to search the bookshelves, as Nikhil no longer read poetry since his marriage, but that he, Sandip, was about to be afflicted with the 'fever fit of poesy' again.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil warned Sandip that he had come to give him a warning.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he was warning him about the 'fever fit of poesy'.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that for some time, Mahomedan preachers had been stirring up the local Mussulmans, who were angry with Sandip and might attack him at any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he had come to advise him to flee.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he had come to give him information, not advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Nikhil that if the estates were his, a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for him, and that Nikhil should intimidate the preachers instead of frightening him, and that Nikhil's weakness was also affecting his neighbouring zamindars.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he had not offered him advice, and that he wished Sandip would refrain from giving him his advice, as it was useless, and that there was another thing he wanted to tell Sandip, namely that Sandip and his followers had been secretly oppressing Nikhil's tenantry, and that he could no longer allow that, so he must ask Sandip to leave his territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he was threatening him with fear of the Mussulmans, or if there was another fear he had to threaten him with.
